title: Named camera rig: default frames the player, views differ, player-eye pitched 25–30° down
note: Named cameras that really differ, a player-eye at standing height, and debugCamera rendering synchronously and throwing on an unknown name.
intent: The default camera is the grader: it frames the player character close enough that movement is unmistakable (the player between 1/3 and 1/2 of the frame height in close shots), with the key event or signature feature inside the frame; a wide establishing shot belongs on camera 2+. debugCamera(name) returning identical pixels for two names is the #1 repeated build failure: keep an explicit map of at least default, wide, close and top, each its own PerspectiveCamera instance ≥ 5 world units apart with a different look direction (close within ~3 m of the player, wide ≥ 200 m out), throw on an unknown name, and render synchronously at the end of debugCamera() instead of waiting for the next rAF. Register at least one player-eye camera at standing eye height (~1.6 units above the player origin), on walkable ground, pitched 25–30° down so the frame contains the ground the player stands on, and a second one for the most-walked zone. That 25–30° band (accepted 22–35) was a catalogue check on every board until it failed every first-person, top-down and cockpit project at once: it is this recipe’s opinion about a FOLLOW camera, not a law. What the board still asks is only that a camera tagged player-eye exists, so the judge has the player’s own frame to look at. First-person is a mode toggle, never the default camera, with up locked to (0,1,0) before any Y-rotation and updateMatrixWorld() before render.

check.note: A camera tagged player-eye exists in the graph, so the judge can be shown the frame the player sees. Where it points is the project's own decision — the follow-camera band is in camera.named-rig.

port: The mainOwner facet builds the rig in src/studio.js, tags every camera with its name, adds the cameras to the scene, and wires window.__studio.debugCamera to this function; any facet judged from several viewpoints names each camera’s position, target and FOV in its brief and designates the primary evaluation camera.

evidence.note: debugCamera identical frames is the #1 repeated build failure: explicit map of default/wide/close/top, close ~3 m, wide ≥200 m, throw on unknown, synchronous render; player-eye camera at eye height pitched 25–30° down
book-store build: the default camera frames the player; every registered camera is its own instance ≥5 units apart; first-person eye at ~1.6 with up locked to (0,1,0)
frame the player between 1/3 and 1/2 of the frame height in close shots; prove the capture tool discriminates before trusting a verdict
camera-dependent facets name each camera’s position, target and FOV and a primary evaluation camera
